claim: SCGB3A2 is a small protein predominantly secreted in airways.
source: secretoglobin(SCGB)3A2, a small protein predominantly secreted in airways
evidence: This is stated directly in the abstract of the manuscript.

claim: SCGB3A2 chaperones LPS to the cytosol through the cell surface receptor syndecan-1.
source: Here we show that secretoglobin(SCGB)3A2, a small protein predominantly secreted in airways, chaperones LPS to the cytosol through the cell surface receptor syndecan-1
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and supported by experimental data throughout the manuscript including binding assays, imaging, and functional studies.

claim: SCGB3A2-mediated LPS delivery leads to pyroptotic cell death driven by caspase-11.
source: this leads to pyroptotic cell death driven by caspase-11
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by experimental data showing caspase-11 activation, pyroptotic morphology, and cell death assays.

claim: SCGB3A2 and LPS co-treatment significantly induced pyroptosis of macrophage RAW264.7 cells.
source: SCGB3A2 and LPS co-treatment significantly induced pyroptosis of macrophage RAW264.7 cells
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by data in Figure 4 showing LDH release and inflammasome activation in RAW264.7 cells.

claim: SCGB3A2 and LPS co-treatment decreased cancer cell proliferation in vitro.
source: SCGB3A2 and LPS co-treatment significantly induced pyroptosis of macrophage RAW264.7 cells and decreased cancer cell proliferation in vitro
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by CCK8 assays shown in multiple figures.

claim: SCGB3A2 treatment resulted in reduced progression of xenograft tumors in mice.
source: while SCGB3A2 treatment resulted in reduced progression of xenograft tumors in mice
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by in vivo metastasis model data shown in Figure 1.

claim: Intracellular LPS triggers the non-canonical inflammasome pathway, resulting in pyroptosis of innate immune cells.
source: Intracellular lipopolysaccharide (LPS) triggers the non-canonical inflammasome pathway, resulting in pyroptosis of innate immune cells.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and is supported by citations to prior work (Hagar et al., 2013; Kayagaki et al., 2013) mentioned in the introduction.

claim: LPS can directly cause regression of some tumors.
source: In addition to its well-known proinflammatory role, LPS can directly cause regression of some tumors, although the underlying mechanism has remained unknown.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and referenced in the introduction with citations to historical work.

claim: TLR4 is a LPS-specific pattern recognition receptor at the cell membrane.
source: It was previously thought that toll-like receptor 4 (TLR4) is the sole LPS-specific pattern recognition receptors (PRRs) at the cell membrane (Poltorak et al., 1998).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a citation to Poltorak et al., 1998.

claim: There is a TLR4-independent mechanism to sense LPS in the cytosol via caspase-11 in a non-canonical inflammasome pathway.
source: However, recent studies demonstrated the presence of an TLR4-independent PRRs mechanism to sense LPS in the cytosol via an inflammatory caspase, caspase-11, in a non-canonical inflammasome pathway (Hagar et al., 2013; Kayagaki et al., 2013).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations to Hagar et al., 2013 and Kayagaki et al., 2013.

claim: SCGB3A2 is abundantly and specifically expressed in non-ciliated airway epithelial (club) cells of the trachea, bronchus, and bronchioles.
source: A cytokine-like small secreted protein, SCGB3A2 (secretoglobin 3A2, also known as UGRP1 and HIN-2), was previously identified that is abundantly and specifically expressed in non-ciliated airway epithelial (club) cells of the trachea, bronchus, and bronchioles (Niimi et al., 2001)
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a citation to Niimi et al., 2001.

claim: SCGB3A2 functions to suppress lung inflammation and fibrosis.
source: revealing that SCGB3A2 functions to suppress lung inflammation and fibrosis (Cai and Kimura, 2015; Cai et al., 2014; Chiba et al., 2006; Kido et al., 2014; Kurotani et al., 2011; Yoneda et al., 2016).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with multiple citations to prior work.

claim: The proliferation of LLC cells was markedly suppressed by mouse recombinant SCGB3A2.
source: The proliferation of LLC cells was markedly suppressed by mouse recombinant SCGB3A2 (Figure 1A).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by CCK8 assay data shown in Figure 1A.

claim: Administration of SCGB3A2 inhibited LLC cell growth in vivo in the intravenous metastasis model.
source: This in vitro effect of SCGB3A2 was also observed in vivo in the LLC cells intravenous metastasis model using wild-type C57BL/6 mice in conjunction with administration of SCGB3A2 (Figure 1B–1E).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by data in Figures 1B-1E showing reduced tumor numbers.

claim: Scgb3a2-null mice developed far greater numbers of lung surface tumors than wild-type littermates when LLC cells were intravenously injected.
source: Mice null for Scgb3a2 developed far greater numbers of lung surface tumors than wild-type littermates when LLC cells were intravenously injected (Figure 1F).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by data in Figure 1F.

claim: Administration of recombinant mouse SCGB3A2 to Scgb3a2-null mice rescued the Scgb3a2-null phenotypes of LLC cell lung metastasis.
source: Furthermore, administration of recombinant mouse SCGB3A2 to Scgb3a2-null mice clearly rescued the Scgb3a2-null phenotypes of LLC cell lung metastasis (Figure 1G–1I).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by data in Figures 1G-1I.

claim: Some sources of recombinant SCGB3A2 had almost no effect on LLC cell growth inhibition.
source: However, we noticed an unexpected phenomenon where some sources of recombinant SCGB3A2 had almost no effect on LLC cell growth inhibition (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by data in Figure 2—figure supplement 1A.

claim: The effect of SCGB3A2 on LLC cell growth inhibition was associated with the level of endotoxin (LPS) contained in the various preparations.
source: This phenomenon was found to be associated with the level of endotoxin (LPS) contained in the various preparations (Supplementary file 1).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by endotoxin measurements in Supplementary file 1.

claim: The growth of LLC cells was strongly inhibited by small amounts of LPS.
source: Indeed, the growth of LLC cells was strongly inhibited by small amounts of LPS (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by CCK8 assay data in Figure 2A.

claim: SCGB3A2 interacted with LPS and dramatically enhanced the electrophoretic mobility of LPS.
source: Pre-incubation with SCGB3A2 (human SCGB3A2 (C1); see Supplementary file 1; unless otherwise noted, this lot was mainly used in the current studies) produced a broad diffuse band in dose dependent manner, indicating that SCGB3A2 interacted with and dramatically enhanced the electrophoretic mobility of LPS (Figure 2B, lane 2–5, and Figure 2C).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by imidazole-zinc staining data in Figures 2B and 2C.

claim: SCGB3A2 directly binds to LPS.
source: To further confirm that SCGB3A2 directly binds to LPS, streptavidin pull-down assays were performed using LPS-Biotin and recombinant SCGB3A2 (Figure 2D). The results clearly showed that SCGB3A2 is an LPS binding protein.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by pull-down assay data in Figure 2D.

claim: SCGB3A2 has the ability to bind and disaggregate LPS micelles.
source: The ability of SCGB3A2 to bind and disaggregate LPS micelles was further demonstrated by the dynamic light scattering (DLS) method (Figure 2E and Figure 2—figure supplement 1C–1E).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by DLS data in Figure 2E and supplementary figures.

claim: Human SCGB3A2(C1) alone showed drastic inhibition of LLC cells growth in vivo.
source: Human SCGB3A2(C1) alone showed drastic inhibition of LLC cells growth, while the amount of LPS contained in the recombinant SCGB3A2 preparation C1 or C3, or high concentration did not show any statistically significant differences in tumor numbers compared with PBS administration (Figure 2F).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by in vivo metastasis data in Figure 2F.

claim: LPS-treated lungs showed much larger lesions than SCGB3A2-treated lung tumors.
source: Moreover, LPS-treated lungs showed much larger lesions than did SCGB3A2-treated lung tumors, which sometimes encompassed the entire lobes, demonstrating the fundamental differences between LPS alone and SCGB3A2 administration (Figure 2G).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by histological images in Figure 2G.

claim: Syndecan-1 (SDC1) showed positive interaction with SCGB3A2 in pull-down assays.
source: To confirm a direct interaction with SCGB3A2, pull-down assays were performed, in which syndecan-1 (SDC1) and podoplanin (PDPN, T1-alpha) showed positive interaction with SCGB3A2 (Figure 3B and data not shown).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by co-immunoprecipitation data in Figure 3B.

claim: SDC1 was moderately expressed in proximal airway epithelial cells.
source: PDPN is known as a marker for alveolar type I epithelial cells in lung, while SDC1 was moderately expressed in proximal airway epithelial cells (Figure 3C)
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by immunostaining data in Figure 3C.

claim: SDC1 was highly expressed on LLC cells surfaces in vitro and in metastatic LLC cells in vivo.
source: SDC1 was found to be highly expressed on LLC cells surfaces in vitro as well as in metastatic LLC cells in vivo (Figure 3D and Figure 3—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by immunofluorescence and IHC data in Figure 3D and supplementary figures.

claim: B16F10 mouse melanoma cell line showed focal expression of SDC1 near cell nuclei and faint staining at cell-to-cell contact sites.
source: In contrast, the B16F10 mouse melanoma cell line, which exhibited less SCGB3A2-dependent growth suppression effects than LLC in vitro (data not shown), showed focal expression of SDC1 near cell nuclei and faint staining at cell-to-cell contact sites (Figure 3D)
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by immunofluorescence data in Figure 3D.

claim: LLC cells stably expressing shRNA-SDC1 showed diminished SCGB3A2 binding.
source: LLC cells stably expressing shRNA-SDC1 (LLC-sh-SDC1, Figure 3—figure supplement 1C) showed diminished SCGB3A2 binding (Figure 3G).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by FACS data in Figure 3G.

claim: ARH-77-mSDC1 enhanced SCGB3A2 binding compared to the parental cells.
source: ARH-77-mSDC1 enhanced SCGB3A2 binding compared to the parental cells (Figure 3—figure supplement 1E).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by FACS data in Figure 3—figure supplement 1E.

claim: Heparin addition significantly inhibited the binding of SCGB3A2 to LLC cells.
source: Heparin addition significantly inhibited the binding of SCGB3A2 to both LLC (Figure 3H) and ARH-77-mSDC1 cells (Figure 3—figure supplement 1F)
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by FACS data in Figure 3H and supplementary figures.

claim: Heparan sulfate on SDC1 may play a role in SCGB3A2 binding.
source: suggesting that HS on SDC1 may play a role in SCGB3A2 binding.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and is an inference based on the heparin inhibition data.

claim: After stimulation with SCGB3A2, SDC1 signal became relatively concentrated on cell protrusions equivalent to the uropod structure.
source: After stimulation with SCGB3A2, the SDC1 signal became relatively concentrated on cell protrusions equivalent to the uropod structure of myeloma (Børset et al., 2000; Yang et al., 2003), which co-localized with SCGB3A2 (Figure 4A,+SCGB3A2).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by immunofluorescence data in Figure 4A.

claim: When LLC cells were incubated with LPS and SCGB3A2, Alexa-labeled LPS, SCGB3A2, and clathrin all co-localized in uropod.
source: Interestingly, when LLC cells were incubated for a short time with LPS and SCGB3A2, Alexa-labeled LPS (LPSA488,Figure 4—figure supplement 1A), SCGB3A2, and clathrin, a key protein for endocytosis, all co-localized in uropod (Figure 4B).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by immunofluorescence data in Figure 4B.

claim: LLC cells appeared to have incorporated SCGB3A2 into the cells as visualized using an HaloTag-SCGB3A2 fusion protein.
source: Upon further incubation, LLC cells appeared to have incorporated SCGB3A2 into the cells as visualized using an HaloTag (HT)-SCGB3A2 fusion protein (Figure 4—figure supplement 1B and C).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by imaging data in Figure 4—figure supplement 1B and C.

claim: The LPS-SCGB3A2 complex enters LLC cells via binding to SDC1 followed by clathrin-dependent endocytosis.
source: suggesting that the LPS-SCGB3A2 complex enters LLC cells via binding to SDC1 followed by clathrin-dependent endocytosis (see below).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and is an inference based on the co-localization and inhibitor data.

claim: SCGB3A2 tends to form oligomers in vitro.
source: In fact, SCGB3A2 tends to form oligomers in vitro, demonstrating the validity of the computer modeling (Figure 4—figure supplement 2G, see Figure 2C CBB staining, also cf: (Cai et al., 2014; Niimi et al., 2001)).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by gel electrophoresis data in Figure 4—figure supplement 2G and citations.

claim: At an early time point, most of the LPS staining was co-localized with EEA1, which was clearly enhanced when cells were co-incubated with SCGB3A2.
source: At an early time point, most of the LPS staining was co-localized with EEA1, which was clearly enhanced when cells were co-incubated with SCGB3A2 (Figure 4D).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by immunofluorescence data in Figure 4D.

claim: At a later time point, some of the LPS staining did not overlap with either EEA1 or LAMP1.
source: At a later time point, however, some of the LPS staining did not overlap with either EEA1 or LAMP1 (Figure 4E).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by immunofluorescence data in Figure 4E.

claim: LPS staining was clearly visible inside the membrane, which differed from the EEA1 distribution pattern.
source: With SDC1 staining depicting the plasma membrane, LPS staining was clearly visible inside the membrane, which differed from the EEA1 distribution pattern (Figure 4F).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by immunofluorescence data in Figure 4F.

claim: LPS could be transported into the cytosol of LLC cells through an SCGB3A2-dependent mechanism.
source: These results suggest that LPS could be transported into the cytosol of LLC cells through an SCGB3A2-dependent mechanism.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and is an inference based on the imaging data showing cytosolic LPS.

claim: SCGB3A2 + LPS increased pro-caspase-11 and NLRP3 in LLC-sh-TLR4 cells.
source: SCGB3A2 + LPS increased pro-caspase-11 and NLRP3, while caspase-1 expression, the major caspase activated by the canonical inflammasome, was not significantly different (Figure 4G).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by western blot data in Figure 4G.

claim: Co-incubation of RAW264.7 cells with SCGB3A2 + LPS clearly enhanced expression of caspase-11 and NLRP3, followed by IL-1β up-regulation and maturation.
source: Co-incubation of RAW264.7 cells with SCGB3A2 + LPS clearly enhanced expression of caspase-11 and NLRP3, followed by IL-1β up-regulation and maturation, while SCGB3A2 or LPS alone did not (Figure 4H).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by western blot data in Figure 4H.

claim: Heparin co-incubation abrogated caspase-11/NLRP3/IL-1β expression by SCGB3A2 + LPS in RAW264.7 cells.
source: Heparin co-incubation abrogated caspase-11/NLRP3/IL-1β expression by SCGB3A2 + LPS.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by western blot data in Figure 4H.

claim: SCGB3A2 enhanced IL-1β secretion from RAW264.7 cells, which was inhibited by the addition of heparin.
source: SCGB3A2 enhanced IL-1β secretion from RAW264.7 cells, which was inhibited by the addition of heparin (Figure 4—figure supplement 4B).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by ELISA data in Figure 4—figure supplement 4B.

claim: RAW264.7 cells exhibited greater cytotoxicity by SCGB3A2 + LPS compared to the individual treatments.
source: A lactate dehydrogenase (LDH) cytotoxicity assay showed that RAW264.7 cells exhibited greater cytotoxicity by SCGB3A2 + LPS compared to the individual treatments, demonstrating the critical role of SCGB3A2 as an LPS delivery molecule to macrophage cells as well (Figure 4—figure supplement 4C).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by LDH assay data in Figure 4—figure supplement 4C.

claim: In LLC cells under SCGB3A2 + LPS, caspase-11 expression was upregulated in a diffused distribution pattern and showed specific foci.
source: In LLC cells under SCGB3A2 + LPS, caspase-11 expression was upregulated in a diffused distribution pattern in the entire area and showed specific foci (Figure 4I).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by immunofluorescence data in Figure 4I.

claim: The caspase-11 foci overlapped with incorporated LPS.
source: Importantly, the caspase-11 foci overlapped with incorporated LPS (Figure 4I).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by immunofluorescence data in Figure 4I.

claim: The expression of NLRP3 was clearly up-regulated by LPS +SCGB3A2 and accumulated around the caspase-11 foci.
source: The expression of NLRP3 was also clearly up-regulated by LPS +SCGB3A2 and accumulated around the caspase-11 foci.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by immunofluorescence data in Figure 4I.

claim: When LPS was introduced into LLC cells using a DNA transfection reagent, LLC cells showed increased intracellular LPS signals and caspase-11 foci, overlapped with LPS.
source: As expected, when LPS was introduced into LLC cells using a DNA transfection reagent, LLC cells showed increased intracellular LPS signals and caspase-11 foci, overlapped with LPS (Figure 4J)
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by immunofluorescence data in Figure 4J.

claim: The formation of caspase-11 foci is mediated by LPS introduction into the cytosol of LLC cells.
source: confirming that the formation of caspase-11 foci is mediated by LPS introduction into the cytosol of LLC cells.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and is an inference based on the LPS transfection data.

claim: Caspase-11 foci formation and NLRP3 upregulation driven by LPS + SCGB3A2 were also observed in RAW264.7 cells.
source: Caspase-11 foci formation and NLRP3 upregulation driven by LPS + SCGB3A2 were also observed in RAW264.7 cells (Figure 4—figure supplement 4D).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by immunofluorescence data in Figure 4—figure supplement 4D.

claim: SCGB3A2 facilitates the delivery of LPS into the cytosol, in concert with the enhancement of non-canonical inflammasome signaling.
source: These results confirm that SCGB3A2 facilitates the delivery of LPS into the cytosol, in concert with the enhancement of non-canonical inflammasome signaling.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and is an inference based on the collective data showing LPS uptake and inflammasome activation.

claim: Dynasore potently inhibited the incorporation of SCGB3A2 and LPS into the cytosol of LLC cells.
source: LLC cells had strong focal staining of SCGB3A2-HT and LPSA448 at the corresponding locations to each other, while Dynasore potently inhibited the incorporation of SCGB3A2 and LPS into the cytosol of LLC cells (Figure 4K)
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by imaging data in Figure 4K.

claim: Dynasore abrogated the activation of caspase-11.
source: and abrogated the activation of caspase-11 (Figure 4L).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by western blot data in Figure 4L.

claim: LDH release from LLC cells was slightly upregulated by LPS +SCGB3A2, while this upregulation was not observed when cells were treated with either Dynasore or Wedelolactone.
source: LDH release from LLC cells as indication for cytotoxicity was slightly upregulated by LPS +SCGB3A2, while this upregulation was not observed when cells were treated with either Dynasore or Wedelolactone (caspase-11 inhibitor) (Kobori et al., 2004) (Figure 4M, Figure 4—figure supplement 5A).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by LDH assay data in Figure 4M and supplementary figures.

claim: LLC-sh-casp-11 cells did not show any significantly different numbers of lung tumors after SCGB3A2 administration.
source: Furthermore, when LLC-sh-casp-11 cells (Figure 4—figure supplement 5B) were subjected to the intravenous metastasis model with or without SCGB3A2 administration, they did not show any significantly different numbers of lung tumors after SCGB3A2 administration, in sharp contrast to the results with control LLC cells (Figure 4N).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by in vivo metastasis data in Figure 4N.

claim: Clathrin-mediated endocytosis of LPS +SCGB3A2 and caspase-11 activation are important for the killing of LLC cells in vivo.
source: These results clearly indicate the importance of clathrin-mediated endocytosis of LPS +SCGB3A2 and caspase-11 activation for the killing of LLC cells in vivo.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and is an inference based on the inhibitor and knockdown data.

claim: The SCGB3A2 + LPS complex promoted pyroptotic cell death morphology in cultured LLC cells.
source: The SCGB3A2 + LPS complex promoted pyroptotic cell death morphology in cultured LLC cells (membrane swelling; Figure 5A).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by microscopy images in Figure 5A.

claim: CCK8 assay confirmed the upregulation of pyroptotic cell death of LLC cells by essentially endotoxin-free SCGB3A2 plus a small amount of LPS.
source: CCK8 assay confirmed the upregulation of pyroptotic cell death of LLC cells by essentially endotoxin-free SCGB3A2 plus a small amount of LPS (Figure 5B).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by CCK8 assay data in Figure 5B.

claim: Flow cytometry analysis revealed the upregulation of propidium iodide (PI) positive cell death by SCGB3A2 + LPS.
source: Furthermore, flow cytometry analysis revealed the upregulation of propidium iodide (PI) positive cell death by SCGB3A2 + LPS (Figure 5C)
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by FACS data in Figure 5C.

claim: SCGB3A2 + LPS induces formation of cell membrane pores, the characteristic feature of pyroptosis.
source: demonstrating the formation of cell membrane pores, the characteristic feature of pyroptosis, induced by SCGB3A2 + LPS.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and is an inference based on the PI staining data.

claim: Large necrotic areas were found in lung tumors from mice treated with early intravenous administration of SCGB3A2.
source: Large necrotic areas were found in lung tumors from mice treated with early intravenous administration of SCGB3A2 (1st and 2nd week) (Figure 5D).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by TUNEL staining data in Figure 5D.

claim: Necrotic areas in lung tumors showed enhanced expression of both caspase-11 and NLRP3.
source: Importantly, these necrotic areas showed enhanced expression of both caspase-11 and NLRP3, demonstrating that tumor cell death occurred through caspase-11-mediated non-canonical inflammasome activation (Figure 5E and F).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by IHC data in Figures 5E and F.

claim: SCGB3A2 significantly promotes pyroptotic death of LLC cells both in vivo and in vitro.
source: These results clearly indicate that SCGB3A2 significantly promotes pyroptotic death of LLC cells both in vivo and in vitro.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and is an inference based on the collective data showing pyroptotic features.

claim: LLC-sh-SDC1 cells showed reduced susceptibility to the cytotoxic effects of LPS +SCGB3A2 complex in vitro.
source: LLC-sh-SDC1 cells showed reduced susceptibility to the cytotoxic effects of LPS +SCGB3A2 complex in vitro (Figure 6A)
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by CCK8 assay data in Figure 6A.

claim: LLC-sh-SDC1 cells showed minimal enhancement of caspase-11 foci formation by LPS +SCGB3A2.
source: accompanied by minimal enhancement of caspase-11 foci formation by LPS +SCGB3A2 (Figure 6B, see Figure 4I).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by immunofluorescence data in Figure 6B.

claim: Heparin addition abrogated the increase of caspase-11 foci in LLC-sh-Control cells.
source: Heparin addition abrogated the increase of caspase-11 foci in LLC-sh-Control cells (Figure 6B)
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by immunofluorescence data in Figure 6B.

claim: Tumor numbers in mice that received LLC-sh-SDC1 cells and SCGB3A2 were not significantly different from those that received LLC-sh-SDC1 cells and PBS.
source: Tumor numbers in mice that received LLC-sh-SDC1 cells and SCGB3A2 were not significantly different from those that received LLC-sh-SDC1 cells and PBS, while tumor numbers with LLC-sh-Control cells were significantly reduced by SCGB3A2 co-injection, similar to that observed in Figure 1 (Figure 6C and D).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by in vivo metastasis data in Figures 6C and D.

claim: SDC1 plays a pivotal role in SCGB3A2-mediated inhibition of LLC cell growth and metastasis in vivo.
source: These experiments confirmed a pivotal role for SDC1 in SCGB3A2-mediated inhibition of LLC cell growth and metastasis in vivo.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and is an inference based on the SDC1 knockdown data.

claim: Casp11, Nlrp3, Aim2, Gsdmd, and Il1b mRNAs were highly expressed only in LLC cells.
source: As a result, Casp11, Nlrp3, Aim2, Gsdmd, and Il1b mRNAs were highly expressed only in LLC cells, suggesting that LLC cells have the machinery to activate a non-canonical inflammasome pathway driven by caspase-11 in combination with higher expression levels of cell surface SDC1 (see Figure 3D and E).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by qPCR data in Figure 6E.

claim: LLC cells have the machinery to activate a non-canonical inflammasome pathway driven by caspase-11 in combination with higher expression levels of cell surface SDC1.
source: suggesting that LLC cells have the machinery to activate a non-canonical inflammasome pathway driven by caspase-11 in combination with higher expression levels of cell surface SDC1 (see Figure 3D and E).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and is an inference based on the gene expression data.

claim: KrasG12D;Scgb3a2(fl/fl) mice clearly showed a poorer survival rate than KrasG12D;Scgb3a2(fl/+) mice.
source: KrasG12D;Scgb3a2(fl/fl) mice clearly showed a poorer survival rate than KrasG12D;Scgb3a2(fl/+) mice.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by survival curve data in Figure 6F.

claim: SCGB3A2 is a member of the secretoglobin family of proteins.
source: SCGB3A2 is a member of the secretoglobin family of proteins, which share a common four helical bundle subunit structure, exist as dimers, tetramers, and other oligomers, and some of which have also been implicated in tumor suppression (Mukherjee et al., 2007) without a clear understanding yet of the mechanistic pathway(s).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section with a citation to Mukherjee et al., 2007.

claim: Some members of the secretoglobin family have been implicated in tumor suppression.
source: which share a common four helical bundle subunit structure, exist as dimers, tetramers, and other oligomers, and some of which have also been implicated in tumor suppression (Mukherjee et al., 2007)
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section with a citation to Mukherjee et al., 2007.

claim: SCGB3A2 functions as an anti-inflammatory and anti-fibrotic agent in the lung.
source: Previously we showed that SCGB3A2 functions as an anti-inflammatory and anti-fibrotic agent in the lung (Cai and Kimura, 2015; Cai et al., 2014; Chiba et al., 2006; Kido et al., 2014; Kurotani et al., 2011; Yoneda et al., 2016).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section with multiple citations to prior work.

claim: A primary function of SCGB3A2 is to protect the hosts from pathogens and pathogen-associated molecular patterns such as LPS.
source: Because SCGB3A2 is mainly secreted by club cells in lung airways, it is reasonable to assume that a primary function of SCGB3A2 is to protect the hosts from pathogens and pathogen-associated molecular patterns such as LPS.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section and is an inference based on the location of SCGB3A2 expression and its function.

claim: SCGB3A2 binds to and facilitates delivery of LPS into the cytosolic compartment through specific binding with SDC1, resulting in cell death via an inflammatory pathway leading to pyroptosis.
source: The current study demonstrated that SCGB3A2 binds to and facilitates delivery of LPS into the cytosolic compartment through specific binding with SDC1, resulting in cell death via an inflammatory pathway leading to pyroptosis.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section and summarizes the main findings of the study.

claim: SCGB3A2 has a conserved role in host defense and enhancing the immune response through the non-canonical inflammasome pathway of pyroptosis.
source: This is commonly seen in the macrophage cell line RAW264.7, suggesting a possible conserved role for SCGB3A2 in host defense and enhancing the immune response through the non-canonical inflammasome pathway of pyroptosis.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section and is an inference based on the data in macrophages.

claim: In LLC cells, the uptake of SCGB3A2-sequestered small amount of LPS triggers inflammatory cell death, probably because of the abundant SDC1 expression on their cell surface.
source: Notably, in the case of LLC cells, the uptake of SCGB3A2-sequestered small amount of LPS triggers inflammatory cell death, probably because of the abundant SDC1 expression on their cell surface.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section and is an inference based on the data showing SDC1 expression and cell death.

claim: Caspase-11 and human caspase-4/5 are specific to mammals.
source: It is noteworthy that caspase-11 and human caspase-4/5 are specific to mammals (Kayagaki et al., 2015)
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section with a citation to Kayagaki et al., 2015.

claim: The SCGB superfamily of proteins, including SCGB3A2, have evolved in mammalian lineages.
source: while the SCGB superfamily of proteins, including SCGB3A2, have also evolved in mammalian lineages (Jackson et al., 2011)
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section with a citation to Jackson et al., 2011.

claim: SCGB3A2 and caspase-11 suggest co-emergent evolution as an 'input-output' for defense from invading pathogens.
source: suggesting the co-emergent evolution as an 'input-output' for defense from invading pathogens.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section and is speculation based on the evolutionary timing of SCGB3A2 and caspase-11.

claim: SDC1 localization to uropods is functionally important as uropods accumulate growth factors and connect them at cell-to-cell contact points or junctions.
source: SDC1 localization to uropods is functionally important as uropods accumulate growth factors and connect them at cell-to-cell contact points or junctions (Børset et al., 2000; Yang et al., 2003).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section with citations to Børset et al., 2000 and Yang et al., 2003.

claim: The SDC1-specific HS sequence is important for targeting SDC1 to uropods.
